record: durable Capture backoff, closed failure classification, installation-wide provider slots and bounded manual retry, source acceptance
evidence_class: deterministic source tests and a local three-process drill on disposable exact-role PostgreSQL 17.11 fixtures (debug build, macOS ARM64, OrbStack Docker 29.4.0) against scripted OpenAI-compatible stubs, plus one source-image, one-node disposable Kind drill against the same stub; not live-provider, published-artifact, multi-node, loaded or production evidence

source.lineages: the published and portable 0016 files are byte-identical; the hard-cut gate accepts the copy and its PostgreSQL 14 syntax scan
source.catalogue_fingerprints: routine 107 rows (Capture transition body replaced), ACL 440 rows (+10 grants) and forced-RLS inventory 137 rows (+1 deployment table without row security) measured by the authority-fingerprints task on the portable lineage; trigger inventory unchanged at 182 rows
source.sqlx_metadata: SYNVEDA_DB_TEST_TASK=sqlx-prepare replaced exactly the nine changed batch/ledger queries and added five new reopen and provider-slot queries; prepare --check passed
source.claim_plan: EXPLAIN on the migrated fixture: the expired branch scans capture_batches_running; the due branch range-scans capture_batches_due on (tenant_id, coalesce(next_attempt_at, created_at)) behind a one-time filter, so it locks no pending row when an expired claim exists

full_suite.tree: the final source tree of this record, after a clean restart of the gate following the last worker change
full_suite.serial_phases: executed, including the published and portable 0015-to-0016 upgrades, the routine and trigger drift suites and the three-process Capture drill under the exact worker login
full_suite.capture_retry_note: the summary counts capture_retry as 7: five cases plus the drill's early return in the general run, which deliberately has no worker login, plus its real serial-phase execution

focused_suites.result: capture_retry 5 passed and capture_api 8 passed, 1 ignored (its serial migrator-lock case runs in the full gate), 0 failed
focused_suites.unit: synveda-ingest 58 lib tests (retry schedule, jitter, Retry-After, status classes, provider identity) and 9 extractor HTTP tests; synveda-types vocabulary round trips; gateway retry-refusal and retry-policy setting tests; console 305 tests
focused_suites.after_full_gate: a test-only assertion that the expired-crash path records terminal_reason=attempts_exhausted was added after the full gate; bash scripts/db-test.sh -p synveda-gateway --test capture_api --test capture_retry -- --test-threads=1 then passed 14, failed 0, ignored 1; make check-api-types and make check-rustdoc passed

local_three_process_drill.topology: one combined and two capture-only synveda-worker processes under the exact worker login; SYNVEDA_CAPTURE_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY=2, lease 4 s, retry base 1 s, maximum delay 2 s, client timeout 10 s
local_three_process_drill.faults: two blocking calls hold both slots; one slot holder is SIGKILLed; 503 and 429 with Retry-After: 1; one call stalled past the client timeout
local_three_process_drill.gate_note: the gate's fixture holds every earlier suite's tenants, so the workers swept many tenants and first claims queued longer than in the isolated run

install.command: CLUSTER=synveda-ops13 KEEP=1 demos/ops-2-helm-install.sh, with KUBECONFIG pointed at a scratch file so no existing context changed
install.cluster: fresh one-node Kind synveda-ops13 (kind v0.32.0, Kubernetes v1.36.1, Helm v4.2.3, CloudNativePG 1.30.0, PostgreSQL 17.11, two CNPG instances); the retained kind-synveda-ops7 release was not touched
install.images: ghcr.io/synveda/product:0.4.7, ghcr.io/synveda/cnpg-postgres:17.11-synveda-0.4.7 and ghcr.io/synveda/keycloak:0.4.7 built from this source by scripts/build-kind-image.sh; product image ID sha256:97901b472e2f711e6d912768b04bd89076be129b335b26f2f2dadca9dddb4c24, re-tagged ops7-capture for the drill workers
install.result: passed: the chart job created a fresh database at schema head 0016 (capture retry schedule), a real authorization-code + PKCE login provisioned the tenant, the governed round trip and audit verification held, the deleted CNPG primary was replaced by synveda-pg-2 and the same context run and worker readiness recovered

kubernetes_drill.topology: three gateway pods, one combined and two Capture-only worker pods from the source image; worker.capture.providerConcurrency=2, retryBaseSeconds=1, retryMaxDelaySeconds=2, extractor.timeoutSeconds=120, default 60-second Capture lease; vLLM-compatible blocking stub in the probe pod; the tenant adopted the canonical team Configuration through the public API because a fresh tenant is fail-safe and admits no external extractor

result.ceiling: two of three batches running with the stub at active=2, maxActive=2, calls=2; the third pending with attempts=0; a worker recorded provider_saturated
result.owner_loss: the slot-holding pod was force-deleted (crash-style); its call closed within the first one-second poll and its slot was refilled 60 s after deletion, one lease, with the stub never above two concurrent calls or three total calls before release
result.completion: all three batches completed with one candidate each; attempts 1,1,2; provider calls 4; maxActive 2; cancelled 1; active 0
result.retry_429: one 429 with Retry-After: 1 produced a persisted next_attempt_at and one retry; attempts 2, one candidate
result.retry_503: one 503 produced a persisted next_attempt_at and one retry; attempts 2, one candidate
result.restore: the script restored the saved Helm values: one gateway, one combined worker, no Capture-only Deployment; no provider slot was held afterwards

earlier_attempts: first run: graceful pod deletion with a 120-iteration wait failed with "the lost owner's slot was not reclaimed after expiry" (214 s)

second run: graceful deletion with a drain-aware deadline failed when the stub saw a fourth call before any slot had expired (134 s); a deleted pod drains for up to worker.shutdownSeconds (75) with its call and slot live, and the default 45-second extractor timeout ended the blocked calls during that drain, so slots returned as ordinary retryable timeouts rather than through lease expiry; leftover rows (two batches completed at attempt 3, one at attempt 4) were consistent with that

after each failed run the cleanup removed the stub while workers still retried, so those batches closed as provider_unreachable / attempts_exhausted or completed after the deterministic extractor returned; no slot stayed held

the passing run deletes the owner with --grace-period=0 --force and raises extractor.timeoutSeconds to 120 for this mode only, so the surviving blocked call outlives one lease and only expiry can free the lost slot
kubernetes_drill.teardown: kind delete cluster --name synveda-ops13 and the scratch kubeconfig were removed after the run

postgres_majors.provisioning: official PostgreSQL images provisioned through the rendered DBA setup script as customer-operated databases
postgres_majors.result: each task exited 0 and printed its compatibility acceptance line (PostgreSQL 14 also refused a 13 server before migration); elapsed 395 s, 235 s, 247 s and 222 s
postgres_majors.capture_suites: capture_api 8 passed, 1 ignored and capture_retry 6 passed, 0 ignored on every major; the exact worker login was supplied, so the three-process drill executed in each run (21.2 to 23.2 s per suite)

not_established: multi-node Kubernetes, rolling mixed-version upgrade and sustained load; the Kind drill is one node, three batches and two injected faults
a live provider, its real rate limits or exactly-once external effects; a repeated attempt can repeat an HTTP call
capacity coordination between separate installations sharing a provider account
owner adoption of the provisional retry, capacity and manual-retry values or a queue-age objective and alert thresholds under load

latency.probe: crates/synveda-gateway/tests/capture_claim_probe.rs (ignored; the identical file ran in a worktree at 3ebabb66)
latency.workload: one tenant with 300 completed batches; 300 idle sweeps, then 150 freeze-and-sweep claims with the deterministic extractor; three alternating rounds per tree, each on a fresh fixture
latency.reading: idle-poll percentiles overlap across rounds; claim-to-completion varies more between rounds of the same tree (baseline p50 19 to 50 ms) than between trees, so this fixture cannot resolve a difference there
latency.round_trips: unchanged for idle polls (7 per tenant: BEGIN, tenant settings, admission lock, tenant read, expired-exhaustion check, claim, ROLLBACK) and for deterministic claims; a provider-bound claim adds 2 statements (ensure and reserve slot) to its claim transaction, 1 to each lease renewal and 1 release to its terminal transaction; a saturated claim rolls back after those statements without a commit
latency.plan: claims and expired-exhaustion checks now use partial indexes over due pending and running rows instead of tenant-wide batch indexes; the benefit at large history or backlog was not measured
latency.limits: debug build, one local Docker PostgreSQL, single process, no concurrent traffic or provider latency; not a production envelope
